rows.statement: Previews Step 92: whether invariants remain true under concurrent multi-agent/multi-process action on shared state, covering Concurrency, Distributed State, Transactions, Consistency, Race Conditions, Event Ordering, Idempotency, Conflict Resolution, Distributed Authorization.

lexical.anchor: We now cross the most important bridge so far ... M_A→M_F→A→I. I ⊨ M_F meaning that the implementation satisfies the formal specification.

conceptual.anchor: 91.30 — Property-based testing ... Instead of testing only examples, we define a property P(x). Then generate many valid and invalid instances.

formal.anchor: We now cross the most important bridge so far ... M_A→M_F→A→I. I ⊨ M_F meaning that the implementation satisfies the formal specification.

operational.anchor: 91.2 — Experiment 1 ... Two database records differ internally (created_at). Mathematical model ignores creation time. Expected: alpha(A)=alpha(B). Result: PASS

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.25 — Example: evidence ... Evidence=(claim,source,time,provenance,confidence). Implementation could use PostgreSQL, Neo4j, event store, object storage, document database. The storage technology is secondary. What matters is whether alpha(I) preserves the required semantics.
rationale_evidence.statement: Worked example: an Evidence abstract tuple (claim,source,time,provenance,confidence) can be stored in any of several technologies; what matters is whether α(I) preserves the required semantics, not the storage technology.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.27 — Domain invariants become executable contracts ... I_Authority: Execute(a) ⇒ Authorized(a). This can become an executable assertion.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues mathematical invariants like I_Authority (Execute(a) ⇒ Authorized(a)) can become executable assertions in the implementation.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.43 — Refinement can introduce implementation detail ... CacheRefresh, MessageQueue, Retry, DatabaseTransaction. These need not appear in the abstract model if they do not change its externally relevant semantics.
rationale_evidence.statement: States concrete-only implementation details (CacheRefresh, MessageQueue, Retry, DatabaseTransaction) need not appear in the abstract model if they preserve externally relevant semantics.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.54 — Domain events ... Instead of direct mutation A→B.internalState, we can have A→DomainEvent→B. This preserves autonomy. But event semantics must be explicit.
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes domain events (A→DomainEvent→B) instead of direct cross-domain state mutation, preserving autonomy while requiring explicit event semantics.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.56 — Type systems as semantic constraints ... ApprovedRequest distinct from DraftRequest. Then a function requiring ApprovedRequest cannot accept a DraftRequest without an explicit transition.
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes using distinct types (ApprovedRequest vs DraftRequest) to encode invariants at the type level, preventing implicit acceptance of the wrong state.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 91.63 — Formal specification versus executable specification ... Policy: Approved∧Authorized ⇒ DeployAllowed. This can be encoded in a policy engine. Specification→ExecutableRule. This reduces semantic drift.
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes encoding formal specifications as executable rules in a policy engine (Specification→ExecutableRule) to reduce semantic drift.

sources.note: The 15/16-document synthesis write-up (2026-09-04/05, indexed by theory-00) presenting the KR-ZERO/KR-REP-REDUCTION/KR-BRIDGE/KR-CONTR/KR-COMP research programme as one status-tagged register: primitives/signatures, the load-bearing Eliminability!=Preservation!=Realization separation, the Zero algebra refutation table, the DPI as the programme's sole theorem, the contradiction/composition lane, the frozen/refuted negative-knowledge register, experimental methodology, statistical inference standards, open questions, and the corrected Focus/Inquiry vs Restriction model. Distinct from (but built on) the individual KR-* experiment objects already indexed; explicitly RESEARCH SYNTHESIS, not Theory v1.3, with Theory v1.2 remaining FROZEN throughout.

rows.anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
rows.statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

experiment.hypothesis: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are separate properties
experiment.setup: KR-REP-REDUCTION, KR-BRIDGE-01/02
experiment.assumptions: small synthetic carrier
experiment.inputs: Zero rate, RD estimates, adequacy/realization measurements
experiment.method: independent measurement of each predicate
experiment.result: three separations each independently evidenced
experiment.interpretation: [EXP] not [THM]
experiment.limitations: scope-bound to tested carrier
experiment.conclusion: three-question separation holds in tested systems

rows.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
rows.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

rows.anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
rows.statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

rows.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
rows.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

rows.anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
rows.statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

rows.anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
rows.statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

rows.anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
rows.statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

rows.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
rows.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

rows.anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
rows.statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

rows.anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
rows.statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

rows.anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
rows.statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

rows.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
rows.statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

rows.anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
rows.statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

rows.anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
rows.statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

rows.anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
rows.statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
rows.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

assumptions.statement: E_S recomputes rank at the relational level in tested implementations
assumptions.anchor: the naive D∖S leaves stale ranks

rows.anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
rows.statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

rows.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
rows.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
rows.statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

rows.anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
rows.statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

rows.anchor: A representation R = T(D) is adequate for Q iff Q is determined by R: Hhat(Q|R)=0
rows.statement: Adequacy is defined information-theoretically as zero conditional entropy of Q given R, operationalized as fiber Q-homogeneity over a population; flagged [DEFECT] contained: adequacy so defined is population-dependent by construction, though checked flat across n=1500/4000/8000.

rows.anchor: N_viol is exact and bias-free
rows.statement: N_viol, the count of conflicting Q-pairs within a representation fiber, is exact and bias-free (unlike the plug-in Hhat estimator with known small-sample bias) and is authoritative for the combinatorial question 'is adequacy exactly zero?'.

rows.anchor: Data-Processing Inequality: for a deterministic sequential chain, H(Q|R5) <= H(Q|R4) <= H(Q|R3) <= H(Q|R2)
rows.statement: The single [THM] in the entire Theory 00-14 register — the standard data-processing inequality, cited not re-derived, stated as the only theorem to make explicit how rare true theorem status is in this research programme.

rows.anchor: a priori impossible ≠ empirically falsified
rows.statement: A hypothesis (H-C, 'adequacy lost at step k and regained at k+j') was first recorded as 'refuted a priori', which was wrong; corrected to 'structurally inapplicable' to a sequential DPI-governed chain, distinguishing an ill-posed hypothesis from an empirically falsified one — recorded as the correction that matters, not pedantry.

rows.anchor: The DPI applies to sequential families. It does not apply to a parallel family
rows.statement: In a parallel family (every Rk=Tk(D) computed directly from D) non-monotone adequacy is perfectly possible; KR-BRIDGE-01/02/03 deliberately used a parallel family for exactly this reason.

rows.anchor: Bytes are FLAT across R5→R3 while cardinality falls 8x. Fields never change.
rows.statement: Reduction is genuinely multi-dimensional: measured bytes stayed at 37.0 from R5 to R4 while distinct-value cardinality fell from 26826 to 5696, refuting any single-scalar measure of 'how much was reduced'.

rows.anchor: The bootstrap confidence interval on Ĥ is invalid in this design.
rows.statement: Resampling with replacement duplicates cases, shrinking fiber diversity and depressing conditional entropy downward, biasing reported bootstrap CIs toward 'adequate'; contained because every adequacy verdict rests on the exact N_viol statistic and train/test splits, not the bootstrap CI.

rows.anchor: OQ-1 — The carrier. blocks everything tactical
rows.statement: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier (every result on r=(value,source,tag,time), |D|<=6); closing it requires a governance decision informed by, not derived from, the experiments — no experiment can decide it.

rows.anchor: DECISION-02: is φ a semantic evaluation frame or an evidence partition?
rows.statement: Blocks the composition rule and the delta transition; experiments constrain but cannot decide it; also decides which bounded context owns phi.

rows.anchor: OQ-4 — Adequacy vs Realization, actually exhibited
rows.statement: Never achieved: requires a level with Hhat(Q|R)=0 and F<1 (a decoder deliberately weaker than the information, or a constraint that bites at an adequate level); flagged as the highest-value experiment available because it is the one separation the programme claims but has never shown.

rows.anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
rows.statement: Standing conjecture with an explicit refutation condition (one substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits); stated so it can be attacked rather than hardening into an assumption.

rows.anchor: Do not promote any [EXP] to [THM]
rows.statement: Explicit recommendation list of what NOT to do next: don't further tune the generator, don't widen the Pi x Q grid, don't declare a 'no-bridge law', don't promote [EXP] to [THM] (a theorem needs a proof not more evidence), don't move to a new algebra/Vedic-derived operator, don't test the Gita strand further for kernel candidacy, and don't open Theory v1.3 before adjudication.

rows.anchor: Theory v1.2 remains FROZEN. The kernel remains NOT SELECTED. No algebra is declared. No carrier is declared.
rows.statement: The standing position closing the Theory 00-14 set: nothing in the thirteen/fifteen-document set is adjudicated; the set exists so that adjudication is now possible.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS requires four-valued logic is NOT supported.
rows.statement: Tested contradiction requirements do not force a fourth flat value; flat candidates A/B/C fail the same seven required distinctions, whose common failure lies in the unknown/boundary family, not contradiction itself — reframing 'the problem that looked like a contradiction problem' as a boundary/unknown problem.

rows.anchor: A structured reason/boundary component is indispensable within the tested candidate representation language.
rows.statement: Wording explicitly softened by measurement, not rewording, from an earlier overclaim that 'reason is the sole indispensable field'; reason-expressivity objection is tested and answered (reason takes 10 values and the finding survives factorization).

rows.anchor: Minimum flat cardinality depends on the declared required-distinction set.
rows.statement: There is no context-free answer to 'how many truth values do we need'; the structural requirement grew the state space from chi=3 to chi=21 but the finding is that cardinality is the wrong axis, not that 21 values are needed.

rows.anchor: The commissioned witness shape does not separate the three [composition] rules. A different shape does — and the commissioned shape eliminates a rule outright instead.
rows.statement: W1 (commissioned witness) eliminates last-wins via a C1 failure on all six surviving triples instead of separating the three rules; W2 (an alternate witness with no internal conflict) separates majority from intraframe-only; C6 order-invariance eliminates last-wins a second time independently — the separating witness must have no internal conflict.

rows.anchor: last-wins is not well-defined on the evidence set — its output depends on enumeration order.
rows.statement: A composition rule must be a function of the evidence set, not of its listing; last-wins is eliminated twice, independently (by W1's C1 failure and by C6 order-invariance).

rows.anchor: K_t → A_t (AttributedState). Knows → True is external and factive; Verification is a separate concern
rows.statement: DECIDED under factivity work (R1): an earlier evaluator returned T for uninterpreted/theory-incomplete states, a defect unfair to the competing candidate; the strengthened evaluator carries an explicit evaluator_exists flag.

rows.anchor: The rank-convention result is NOT a further instance [of DECISION-01].
rows.statement: DECISION-01 ('semantic evaluation must be invariant under non-evidential variation') is RATIFIED, but the rank-convention reading required an invertible recoding that the audit refuted with 21369 tie violations; the claim was withdrawn by both the original author and the review's replacement wording.

rows.anchor: DECISION-02 — Is φ a semantic evaluation frame, or an evidence partition? OPEN, and blocking
rows.statement: The single largest open governance item in the contradiction/composition lane: nothing downstream may be settled by inference from experiments, which only constrain, not decide, it.

rows.anchor: Pairwise semantic/evidential distinguishability cannot carry family-level epistemic complexity by itself.
rows.statement: FR-001, FROZEN 2026-09-02 as a research-result freeze (not a theory/architecture decision), established by two independent failure mechanisms: sim_Lambda is not transitive (sorites witness spanning 3.068 at delta=0.3099) and the transitivity-free delta-packing repair captures redundancy but fails on coupling (correlated up to 222x); KR-HILBERT's spectral route strengthened rather than reopened the freeze.

rows.anchor: reason is the sole indispensable field
rows.statement: FR-002 explicitly withheld from freezing (CANDIDATE, NOT FROZEN) pending re-check of this exact wording, since softened and tested by measurement; the candidate list stands but the freeze does not.

rows.anchor: Read-disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T) and verified empirically.
rows.statement: FR-003, CANDIDATE this cycle, established by KR-BRIDGE-02 §2 catching a false positive (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) that a hand-inspected provenance map (wrong twice) would otherwise have let through; needs a second independent adopter before promotion per ES-006.1.

rows.anchor: individual Zero ⟹ group Zero [and converse] ... [NEG] (both directions)
rows.statement: The refutation ledger of Zero-algebra claims: L is not a projection, L is not confluent, individual<=>group Zero fails both directions (131 and 63 violations), Z is not down/up/union/intersection-closed as a standard regime, Z is not a matroid, Z is not generated by its minimal elements, and relational transformations are not necessary for higher-order Zero.

rows.anchor: Zero predicts preservation [NEG] — 4 independent tests
rows.statement: Refuted claims about the bridge: Zero does not predict preservation (4 independent tests), Zero does not mark the reduction boundary, admissibility is a property of (Pi,Q,T) not (Pi,Q), read-disjointness cannot be established by declaration, and neither flattening the redundancy distribution nor raising population size increases informative strata.

rows.anchor: Claims withdrawn by their author, which is a separate category
rows.statement: A distinct register from refutation-by-opponent: five self-withdrawn claims are listed (an unproven ordering claim, the KR-BRIDGE-01 single-mechanism explanation superseded by two causes at r=2, a 'representation class is flat' claim overturned by a generator defect where 40.2% of cases bypassed mk(), the section-5 rank headline refuted by audit FAIL 2.3, and 'H-C refuted a priori' corrected to structurally inapplicable), kept visible so retraction is not quietly forgotten.

rows.anchor: The strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence.
rows.statement: The rule this whole frozen/refuted register document enforces, with its operational form: keep facts, architectural conclusions, governance decisions, engineering actions and operational observations rigorously separate — never let one silently become another.

rows.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
rows.statement: KR-BRIDGE-01 (Outcome A): a large marginal association (pooled RD=-0.363) dissolved under stratification, explained by redundancy as a confounder within one informative stratum/carrier/Pi/Q/transformation; tightened on review to forbid stating it as a general causal law.

rows.anchor: The one substantial effect in the entire grid was an artifact of shared reads.
rows.statement: KR-BRIDGE-02's instrument failed twice before reporting anything: first a marginal-RD adjudication falsely reported 'H2 SUPPORTED, 27/27 replicate' (re-finding the known confounder), then a naive read-disjointness gate let through an inadmissible cell (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) caused by rank=f(value,tag) leaking into Pi; a second, corrected gate was itself found unsound by perturbation testing (Pi_arity effectively reading value via dedup survivorship), yielding the rule 'admissibility is a property of the TRIPLE (Pi,Q,T), never of the pair' and 'declaration is not verification.'

rows.anchor: CELLS ACTUALLY SEARCHED: 31 of 112
rows.statement: Final KR-BRIDGE-02 tally: 112 cells, 14 excluded by gate, 67 with no informative stratum, 15 with RD_within=0, 2 non-replicating, 14 survivors of which 0 were substantive on both splits, 1 borderline, 13 negligible; H1 not refuted, with 12 of 14 survivors having no stratum whose 95% CI excluded zero.

rows.anchor: Flattening the redundancy distribution does not increase informative strata
rows.statement: KR-BRIDGE-03 found flattening the redundancy distribution moved informative strata only 73->75 because flattening moves mass into deterministic extremes (r=0: Zero never fires; r=3: Zero always fires) that cannot be informative by construction; the effective lever instead is record count (73->233 at n_rec 4->6), while population size is not a lever (73/74/70 at n=1500/4000/8000).

rows.anchor: 67 dead cells, in every one of the nine regimes. The count did not move by one.
rows.statement: Cause identified as adequacy saturation (most (T,Q) pairs fully preserve or fully destroy Q, 25-31 of 35 combinations sitting at 0.00 or 1.00), a property of the adequacy definition rather than the generator, evidenced across nine regimes; the remaining lever is (T,Q) designs that partially preserve each Q.

rows.anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
rows.statement: Standing conjecture stated with an explicit refutation condition (a single substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits, gate passed, stratum CI excluding zero); explicitly not a law given one carrier family and 31 of 112 cells searched.

rows.anchor: Zero is contract-relative. ... Zero is reference-relative.
rows.statement: KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA H8: 495 of 4049 tested pairs change their Zero verdict under a contract-detail change; H7: 541 of 4260 differ under a reference change — eliminability is not intrinsic to the data.

rows.anchor: L is not a projection. The tested algebra is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process.
rows.statement: Across H1-H11: idempotence is operator-relative (PARTIAL), commutativity fails (11/1162 non-commuting), termination and monotone-decreasing iteration hold, individual<=>group Zero fails both directions (131 and 63 violations), reference/contract invariance fail (541/4260, 495/4049), invariant != Zero (1865 vs 858 mismatches), Remainder=D-Eliminated fails for the transformation residual (equality only 816/1182), and RuleEliminable != CounterfactualZero (55.75% agreement) — which normal form you halt at depends on elimination order.

rows.anchor: Z is NOT generated upward by its minimal elements — 286 / 826 failures
rows.statement: Set-structure closure properties of Zero-subsets Z mostly fail (downward-closed, upward-closed, union-closed all refuted; intersection-closed refuted by only 2 cases and fits exactly once a cancelling contract is removed; not a matroid); the practical consequence is there is no compact generator-based encoding of eliminability — caching minimal eliminable sets and expanding them upward will be wrong.

rows.anchor: "Not eliminated" IS exactly "contract-relevant unresolved material" — a genuine and non-obvious identity, holding without exception in the tested space.
rows.statement: The positive result inside the refuted H10: of three candidate 'Remainder' constructions (D-Eliminated, transformation residual, contract-unresolved material), A and C agree exactly in 1182/1182 tested cases while B (the transformation residual) is a different object agreeing with the others only 816/1182 times — 'the residue of the operation is not the residue of the concern.'

rows.anchor: the eliminability ladder reaches at least k = 3
rows.statement: Demonstrated empirically for n<=6 that some sets are eliminable only as a triple, not pairwise; k>3 is explicitly OPEN and n<=6 is a design bound, not a property of eliminability; the phenomenon is transformation-specific (T2_dedup 28.2% higher-order rate vs T7 exactly 0%), and relational transformations are shown to produce but not be necessary for higher-order Zero.

rows.anchor: One elimination in six is prevented by boundary information alone
rows.statement: Direct empirical support (provenance, uncertainty, scope, contradiction state) for treating boundary/provenance as load-bearing rather than metadata, described as the strongest link from the Zero lane to the kernel design.

rows.anchor: Eliminability ≠ Preservation ≠ Realization ... [EXP] — separated experimentally by KR-ZERO, KR-REP-REDUCTION and KR-BRIDGE-01/02. Not [THM]
rows.statement: Immediate application §4: the standing 2026-09-04 register is fully re-tagged under the new vocabulary, including the DPI as the sole [THM], its [COR] with the corrected 'structurally inapplicable != empirically falsified' note, FR-001 and FR-003 tagged [EXP], and the flattening-redundancy-increases-informative-strata claim explicitly re-tagged [NEG] per the KR-BRIDGE-03 calibration.

rows.anchor: labels are pre-registered classifications, not established facts.
rows.statement: Amendment A1, originating from KR-BRIDGE-01's T_B label mismatch: after execution a pre-registered label (e.g. 'lossy') is verified against observed behaviour and a mismatch is a recorded finding, never silently redefined to match its label.

rows.anchor: do not tune the generator to balance cells. Natural imbalance is evidence.
rows.statement: Amendment A2: cells are reported with their structural cause, never engineered, because balancing an imbalanced four-way table would destroy the information that the imbalance itself was the finding.

rows.anchor: Control A1 is the one that earned its place this cycle.
rows.statement: A ten-control checklist (preserving/destroying/invertible-recoding/four-way-non-degeneracy/separation/Zero-fires-selectively/gate-bites/Pi-not-inert/Q-not-inert/provenance-verified-by-perturbation); Control A1 (perturbation-verified provenance) caught two hand-written provenance maps that were wrong, which code review had not caught.

rows.anchor: Distinguish structurally inapplicable from empirically refuted
rows.statement: Originating from hypothesis H-C being wrongly recorded as 'refuted' when it was actually ill-posed against a sequential DPI-governed design; crediting the experiment with a result it could not have produced would be a false result in the negative direction.

rows.anchor: the check discriminates; it does not merely dissolve.
rows.statement: The generalized provenance check both dissolved the KR-ZERO-GROUP 'case J' finding (revealed as a property of cancelling contracts, not of Zero) and confirmed/strengthened the interaction-order finding (which came out higher without the cancelling contract) — the contrast is evidence the check is a real instrument, not a way to disbelieve inconvenient results.

rows.anchor: Engineering supplies evidence and never accepts its own work
rows.statement: The governance order EXPERIMENT -> AUDIT -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 is stated as part of the method itself, with no shortcuts: evidence, recommendation, and authority stay separate.

rows.anchor: the frontier has moved past my package. Theory 13 ... its top three items are not on my list at all
rows.statement: Concedes that Theory 13's OQ-1 (the carrier), OQ-2 (DECISION-02) and OQ-3 (the transfer problem, 'the largest scientific risk in the programme') supersede the author's own prior gap register as the corpus's authoritative open-question list, concluding 'the estate is blocked on two DECISIONS, not on derivations. My verdict said the opposite.'

rows.anchor: RESEARCH SYNTHESIS. Not Theory v1.3. Not a ratification. Theory v1.2 remains FROZEN · the kernel remains NOT SELECTED · nothing here is adjudicated.
rows.statement: Frames the whole 00-14(+03a) document set's governance status: it sits at the end of AUDIT in the EXPERIMENT->AUDIT->ADJUDICATION->THEORY v1.3 order and exists to make adjudication possible, not to constitute it.

rows.anchor: We have experimentally separated three things that the theory previously mixed: information elimination, preservation of a business inquiry, and successful realization by a decoder.
rows.statement: States the single most important sentence of the set (Eliminability != Preservation != Realization) and clarifies it is [EXP] not [THM]: no proof the three must differ in general, only demonstration that they do differ in every system tested; explicitly not 'we discovered a new algebra' since the algebra experiments were largely negative.

rows.anchor: r = (value, source, tag, timestamp), |D| ∈ {4,5,6} ... Nothing here has been shown to transfer to documents, claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal states or evidence.
rows.statement: States the scope bound inherited by every document in the set: every [EXP] is bounded to this carrier, this Q, this chain, this contract, this value domain; the canonical illustration given is that 'three significant digits is the universal preservation limit' may never be said — only that rounding crossed the observed preservation boundary for this specific carrier/Q/chain/contract/domain.

rows.anchor: Recounted 2026-09-06 across all 16 documents. ⚠️ These are TAG OCCURRENCES, counted mechanically — not distinct statements.
rows.statement: A tag-occurrence ledger for the whole set: [EXP] 129, [NEG] 118, [REC] 40, [OPEN] 34, [DEF] 24, [CONJ] 13, [DEFECT] 11, [THM] 8 (referencing one distinct theorem, the DPI, cited eight times), [COR] 6, [PRP] 3, [CORPUS]/[DESIGN] 1/1; the near-1:1 [NEG]-to-[EXP] ratio is read as the point, not the totals — a set where [EXP] outran [NEG] by an order of magnitude would indicate a programme that had stopped testing its own hypotheses.

rows.statement: Not more experiments but adjudication, requiring at minimum: a carrier decision, resolution of DECISION-02, a second independent FR-003 adopter per ES-006.1, and an explicit governance statement of which scope-bound [EXP] results the theory is willing to depend on.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
rationale_evidence.statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
rationale_evidence.statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
rationale_evidence.statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
rationale_evidence.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Minimum flat cardinality depends on the declared required-distinction set.
rationale_evidence.statement: There is no context-free answer to 'how many truth values do we need'; the structural requirement grew the state space from chi=3 to chi=21 but the finding is that cardinality is the wrong axis, not that 21 values are needed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Flattening the redundancy distribution does not increase informative strata
rationale_evidence.statement: KR-BRIDGE-03 found flattening the redundancy distribution moved informative strata only 73->75 because flattening moves mass into deterministic extremes (r=0: Zero never fires; r=3: Zero always fires) that cannot be informative by construction; the effective lever instead is record count (73->233 at n_rec 4->6), while population size is not a lever (73/74/70 at n=1500/4000/8000).

aliases: Uncertainty Calculus, Probability, Confidence, Belief, Evidence Weighting and the Mathematics of Unknown

sources.note: S0920's Step 27: the fully worked multidimensional uncertainty calculus (eight uncertainty types, Unknown!=0.5, imprecise/interval probability, Dempster-Shafer ignorance) explicitly rejecting a universal confidence score; extends B0021's uncertainty-taxonomy-typed-propagation (S0877/Step 20) with formal Bayes/likelihood/confidence-vs-credible-interval machinery and missing-data-mechanism treatment.

rows.anchor: probably true, high confidence, evidence is weak, we don't know, two plausible explanations, probability is 70% ... not interchangeable ... do not introduce one universal confidence number
rows.statement: Lists six common uncertainty expressions as not interchangeable, recommending against one universal confidence number.

rows.anchor: Truth, Evidence, Probability, Belief, Confidence, Uncertainty ... describe different things ... should not collapse into one scalar
rows.statement: Separates six distinct concepts (Truth, Evidence, Probability, Belief, Confidence, Uncertainty), worked with three contrasting example statements, none collapsible into one scalar.

rows.anchor: P(H)=0.7\neq Truth(H)=0.7 ... The probability describes our uncertainty, not a fractional truth value
rows.statement: States P(H)=0.7 ≠ Truth(H)=0.7 — probability describes uncertainty, not fractional truth.

rows.anchor: epistemic uncertainty ... uncertainty because we do not know enough. More evidence may reduce it
rows.statement: Defines epistemic uncertainty as lack of sufficient evidence, reducible by more evidence.

rows.anchor: Aleatoric uncertainty ... genuine variability ... even with perfect knowledge ... cannot necessarily eliminate randomness
rows.statement: Defines aleatoric uncertainty as inherent process variability not eliminable by more observation, worked with a network-traffic example.

rows.anchor: P(Failure)=0.1 ... Epistemic: we don't know enough ... Aleatoric: the process itself has approximately 10% failure probability ... require different responses
rows.statement: Worked example showing the same P(Failure)=0.1 admits epistemic and aleatoric interpretations requiring different responses.

rows.anchor: 40\pm1\% ... measurement uncertainty ... different from P(ServiceFailure) ... MeasurementUncertainty\neq OutcomeUncertainty
rows.statement: Defines measurement uncertainty, distinct from outcome uncertainty.

rows.anchor: M_1,M_2,M_3 all plausible ... ModelChoice ... model uncertainty ... should not automatically be treated as ordinary sampling uncertainty
rows.statement: Defines model uncertainty (choice among plausible models), distinct from ordinary sampling uncertainty.

rows.anchor: Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X+\epsilon ... SE(\hat\beta_1) ... parameter uncertainty ... distinct from model uncertainty
rows.statement: Defines parameter uncertainty via a regression coefficient standard error, distinct from model uncertainty.

rows.anchor: Approved ... technically approved; architecturally approved; management-approved; conditionally approved ... semantic uncertainty ... A probability over the technical outcome does not solve it
rows.statement: Defines semantic uncertainty (ambiguous term meaning), not resolvable by a probability over the technical outcome.

rows.anchor: nexus-prod and nexus3 ... P(Entity_A=Entity_B) could represent identity uncertainty ... not the same as outcome probability
rows.statement: Defines identity uncertainty via a probability over entity sameness, distinct from outcome probability.

rows.anchor: t\in[10:00,11:00] ... should not arbitrarily select t=10:30 ... temporal uncertainty
rows.statement: Defines temporal uncertainty about an event's exact time, warning against arbitrary point selection.

rows.anchor: P(Failure\mid Deployment) ... P(Failure\mid do(Deployment)) ... Uncertainty about causal structure is different from uncertainty about the probability distribution
rows.statement: Defines causal uncertainty as distinct from probability-distribution uncertainty.

rows.anchor: U(H)=(U_{measurement},U_{epistemic},U_{aleatoric},U_{model},U_{semantic},U_{identity},U_{temporal},U_{causal}) ... not every proposition needs every component
rows.statement: Defines a formal eight-component uncertainty vector, not every proposition requiring every component.

rows.anchor: Confidence=0.85 ... source is highly reliable; model predicts 85%; evidence is strong; identity is 85% likely; human reviewer is confident ... UniversalConfidenceScore=ArchitecturalAntiPattern
rows.statement: Argues a bare confidence score is ambiguous across at least five distinct meanings — UniversalConfidenceScore = ArchitecturalAntiPattern.

rows.anchor: P(H)\in[0,1] and P(H)+P(\neg H)=1 ... we should only assign probabilities when the semantics are clear
rows.statement: Defines probability formally, requiring clear semantics before assignment.

rows.anchor: P(Failure)=0.73 is meaningless without knowing population; conditions; time horizon; model; data; assumptions ... P(H\mid C,M,E,t)
rows.statement: Requires probability to carry context, formalized as P(H|C,M,E,t).

rows.anchor: P(Failure\mid Version=3.69,Load>80\%) ... much more meaningful than P(Failure)=0.1
rows.statement: Prefers conditional probability over unconditional probability for meaningfulness.

rows.anchor: P(SecurityIncident)=0.01 ... Sensitivity=0.95, FalsePositiveRate=0.05 ... a positive signal does not imply P(Incident\mid Positive)=0.95 ... must apply Bayes theorem
rows.statement: Worked base-rate-neglect example: a positive detector signal does not directly give the posterior incident probability without Bayesian correction.

rows.anchor: P(H\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid H)P(H)}{P(E)} ... Prior+Evidence\rightarrow Posterior. This fits KnowledgeOS naturally
rows.statement: States Bayes' theorem giving a principled prior+evidence->posterior update fitting KnowledgeOS naturally.

rows.anchor: Belief_{new}(H)\propto Likelihood(E\mid H)\times Belief_{old}(H) ... we should not require every KnowledgeOS inference to be Bayesian
rows.statement: Defines a KnowledgeOS Bayesian-update form, explicitly not required for every inference — one tool among several.

rows.anchor: EvidenceStrength=High ... does not automatically mean P(H)=0.95 ... relevance; independence; reliability; specificity; authority; temporal validity ... EvidenceAssessment\neq Probability
rows.statement: States EvidenceAssessment ≠ Probability: evidence strength depends on six listed factors, distinct from a model-dependent probability.

rows.anchor: L(H;E)=P(E\mid H) ... not itself P(H\mid E) ... this distinction is essential
rows.statement: Defines Likelihood L(H;E)=P(E|H), distinct from the posterior P(H|E).

rows.anchor: P(E\mid H_1)=0.9 and P(E\mid H_2)=0.8 ... without priors P(H_1),P(H_2), we cannot calculate the posterior probabilities
rows.statement: Worked example showing evidence favoring one hypothesis via likelihood alone, but posteriors requiring priors that aren't given.

rows.anchor: BF_{12}=\frac{P(E\mid H_1)}{P(E\mid H_2)} ... nine times as likely under H_1 than H_2 ... useful for evidence comparison
rows.statement: Defines Bayes factors for hypothesis comparison.

rows.anchor: CMDB, Monitoring, Dashboard, Report all derive from the same underlying database ... EvidenceCount\neq IndependentEvidenceCount ... directly connects to 25X
rows.statement: Worked example warning against treating four commonly-sourced reports as four independent observations — EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount, connecting to Step 25X.

rows.anchor: If Origin(E_1)=Origin(E_2), they may not constitute independent corroboration ... preserve source lineage
rows.statement: Requires an independence graph preserving source lineage to determine plausible pairwise independence.

rows.anchor: 95% confidence interval is not There is a 95% probability that the fixed parameter lies inside this interval ... avoid casual use of 95% Confidence unless the statistical semantics are explicitly defined
rows.statement: Warns against the common misinterpretation of a frequentist confidence interval, requiring explicit statistical semantics before casual '95% Confidence' language.

rows.anchor: CI_{95\%}=[L,U] ... a procedure with a long-run coverage property under assumptions. It is not simply a subjective probability distribution
rows.statement: Formally defines a confidence interval as a long-run-coverage procedure, not a subjective probability distribution.

rows.anchor: P(\theta\in[L,U]\mid E)=0.95 [Bayesian credible interval] ... ConfidenceInterval\neq CredibleInterval. KnowledgeOS must preserve the distinction
rows.statement: Defines the Bayesian credible interval as a genuinely different statement from a confidence interval — ConfidenceInterval ≠ CredibleInterval.

rows.anchor: FailureRate=0.073842 ... may be misleading [with sparse data] ... FailureRate\in[0.04,0.11] ... preserves uncertainty
rows.statement: Prefers an interval estimate over false-precision point estimates when data are sparse.

rows.anchor: L\le P(H)\le U ... 0.4\le P(H)\le0.7 ... useful when evidence is insufficient to specify one exact probability
rows.statement: Defines bounded probability P(H) in [L,U] for cases where a single distribution cannot be justified.

rows.anchor: P(H)\in\mathcal P ... a set of plausible probability distributions ... particularly appropriate for KnowledgeOS where evidence is heterogeneous
rows.statement: Defines imprecise probability as a set of plausible distributions, useful for heterogeneous KnowledgeOS evidence.

rows.anchor: I would not make imprecise probability the universal representation ... Mathematical sophistication\neq architectural quality
rows.statement: Explicitly declines to make imprecise probability the universal representation — Mathematical sophistication ≠ architectural quality; introduce advanced formalisms only where needed.

rows.anchor: Infrastructure may use AvailabilityProbability. Governance may use EvidenceStatus. Identity may use MatchProbability. Architecture may use ApplicabilityStatus ... should not all be forced into ConfidenceScore
rows.statement: States uncertainty semantics belong to the bounded context, worked with four domain-specific examples rather than one forced ConfidenceScore.

rows.anchor: \{Unverified,PartiallyVerified,Verified,Contradicted,Superseded\} ... often more useful than Confidence=0.83
rows.statement: Defines a five-value categorical EvidenceStatus enum for governance, preferred over a confidence number.

rows.anchor: EpistemicStatus could include Observed, Supported, Inferred, Hypothesized, Disputed, Unknown, Rejected, Superseded ... semantic states, not probabilities
rows.statement: Defines an eight-value EpistemicStatus enum as semantic states, not probabilities.

rows.anchor: Assertion: Migration succeeds. Epistemic status: Forecast. Probability: 0.82. Model: RiskModel v4. Horizon: 30 days ... much richer than confidence=82%
rows.statement: Worked example showing probability and epistemic status coexisting in one richer record.

rows.anchor: Unknown ... Not P(H)=0.5 ... 0.5 is a substantive probabilistic claim ... Unknown means we do not possess a justified probability model
rows.statement: Defines Unknown as distinct from P(H)=0.5, since 0.5 is itself a substantive probabilistic claim requiring justification.

rows.anchor: Unknown\neq0.5 ... one of the strongest conclusions of Step 27
rows.statement: States the invariant Unknown ≠ 0.5, called one of the strongest conclusions of Step 27.

rows.anchor: Database version: unknown ... would be wrong to encode Version=0 ... Probability=0.5 is not a valid generic encoding of missing knowledge
rows.statement: Warns against encoding missing data as a default zero or a default 0.5 probability.

rows.anchor: Missing, Unknown, NotApplicable, NotObserved, Withheld, Contradictory ... A SQL NULL alone cannot express all of these semantics
rows.statement: Defines a six-value null-semantics taxonomy that a single SQL NULL cannot express.

rows.anchor: MCAR, MAR, MNAR ... The reason data are missing can itself affect inference ... may become relevant to KnowledgeOS analytics
rows.statement: Introduces the statistical missing-data-mechanism taxonomy (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) as potentially relevant to KnowledgeOS analytics.

rows.anchor: failed deployments are less likely to be logged ... P(Failure\mid Logged) may differ from P(Failure) ... KnowledgeOS must not assume missing evidence is neutral
rows.statement: Worked missing-not-at-random example warning that missing evidence must not be assumed neutral.

rows.anchor: users report only serious incidents ... ObservedIncidentRate>TrueIncidentRate ... selection bias ... depends not only on what was observed, but how the observation process was generated
rows.statement: Worked selection-bias example: evidence quality depends on the observation-generating process, not only on what was observed.

rows.anchor: ObservationProcess ... World\rightarrow ObservationMechanism\rightarrow ObservedEvidence ... can itself introduce bias
rows.statement: Models an explicit ObservationProcess that can itself introduce bias.

rows.anchor: humans document unusual failures more often than normal successes ... KnowledgeOS corpus may overrepresent failure cases ... FailureRate that is much too high
rows.statement: Worked AI-corpus example: documentation bias toward unusual failures can cause the system to overestimate failure rates.

rows.anchor: Q(E,q)=(Reliability,Relevance,Independence,Completeness,Freshness,Provenance) ... Q is not necessarily a probability
rows.statement: Defines a six-dimension evidence-quality vector, explicitly not itself a probability.

rows.anchor: Bayesian updating; likelihood ratios; deterministic rules; expert weighting; Dempster-Shafer-style evidence structures; interval probabilities ... The bounded context determines the appropriate method
rows.statement: Lists six evidence-aggregation methods, with the bounded context determining the appropriate one.

rows.anchor: Support(\{H_1,H_2\}) without assigning separate probabilities ... represents ignorance more explicitly than P(H_1)=0.5
rows.statement: Introduces a Dempster-Shafer-style representation assigning support to a set of hypotheses without distinguishing among them, worked with a Network-vs-Database cause example, explicitly aligned with Unknown≠50%.

rows.anchor: Mathematical sophistication\neq architectural quality ... introduce advanced uncertainty formalisms only where they solve a demonstrated problem
rows.statement: Restates the caution against over-formalizing uncertainty, introducing advanced formalisms only where they solve a demonstrated problem.

rows.anchor: U_D=U_E+U_M+U_P+U_C+U_S ... need not be numerically additive ... the important point is diagnostic separation
rows.statement: Defines a five-term decision-uncertainty decomposition, explicitly not required to be numerically additive — valued for diagnostic separation.

rows.anchor: If U_E is high: acquire better evidence. If U_M is high: evaluate competing models. If U_S is high: clarify terminology. If U_C is high: conduct causal analysis ... Different uncertainty requires different action
rows.statement: Maps each uncertainty-decomposition component to a distinct remedial action.

rows.anchor: NextBestInformation=argmax_O VOI(O) ... connects Step 27 directly to 25Z and 26
rows.statement: Defines NextBestInformation as the VOI-maximizing observation, connecting to Steps 25Z and 26.

rows.anchor: EU(a)=\sum_s P(s\mid E)U(a,s) ... a^*=\arg\max_a EU(a) subject to governance constraints
rows.statement: Restates expected-utility decision-making subject to governance constraints.

rows.anchor: EU(a_1)>EU(a_2) but a_1 has catastrophic downside. Risk constraints may override expected utility ... Decision=Optimization+Constraints+Governance. Not pure mathematics
rows.statement: Restates that risk constraints can override raw expected-utility ranking, giving Decision=Optimization+Constraints+Governance.

rows.anchor: a^*=\arg\max_a\min_{P\in\mathcal P}EU_P(a) ... a robust decision criterion ... not universally appropriate, but useful where probability estimates are unreliable
rows.statement: Defines a robust/minimax decision criterion for unreliable probability estimates, explicitly not universally appropriate.

rows.anchor: p<0.15\Rightarrow Upgrade. p\ge0.15\Rightarrow StageFirst ... Upgrade is recommended if failure probability remains below 15%; above that threshold, staged migration dominates ... far more useful to an architect
rows.statement: Worked sensitivity-analysis example identifying a decision-flipping probability threshold, making the recommendation transparent and conditional rather than a bare directive.

rows.statement: Runs nine falsification tests (A-I, all PASS) against the uncertainty-calculus model: an Unknown epistemic status does not automatically get assigned a probability; high-quality but off-target evidence yields Relevance=False; two same-source reports yield IndependentEvidenceCount=1; a probability computed outside model applicability yields ProbabilityStatus=NotApplicable; measurement uncertainty is not automatically converted into an outcome-probability claim; semantic ambiguity yields SemanticUncertainty rather than a fabricated numerical confidence; evidence-indistinguishable hypotheses yield Underdetermined or a set-valued belief rather than an automatic 50/50 split; a high-value discriminating observation can dominate immediate action; and a historically-revised probability leaves both old and new values historically accessible.

sources.note: A full structural reading of Kenneth Williams Vedic Math Genius (distinct book from the Bharati Krishna Tirtha material behind vedic-mathematics-candidate-transformation-algebra, though closely related in theme): extracts reference-relative representation, compensation, complement/involution, local+interaction decomposition, carrying/propagation, duplex interaction terms, deficiency, scale transformation, execution-order independence, state cycles, residual-carrying transformations, representation-switching, representative-value abstraction, five distinct zero-like mechanisms (cancellation/residual-disappearance/proportional-explanation/completion/complement), closure, sufficient statistics, invariants, and combinatorial composition; reclassifies all sixteen sutras structurally; proposes hypothesis KR-ALGEBRA-H1 (a seven-part representation-relative transformation algebra in which Zero emerges rather than being primitive) and experiment KR-ALGEBRA-01 (a ten-property transformation test battery); closes with a historical-claim-vs-mathematical-evidence caution and a three-sub-lane KR-ALGEBRA research programme.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Grid Multiplication: n^2 mults, n^2 additions standard vs n^2 mults, n(n-1) additions Vedic, Theta(n^2). Base Multiplication: 4 mults/2 additions standard vs 1 mult/3 additions Vedic, Theta(1) near base / Theta(n^2) general. Duplex Squaring: n^2 mults standard vs n(n+1)/2 mults Vedic, Theta(n^2). Th
rationale_evidence.statement: Delivers a critical complexity-theory correction to a common overclaim about Vedic Mathematics: a three-method complexity comparison table shows Vedic methods never change the asymptotic complexity class (grid multiplication and duplex squaring remain Theta(n^2), strictly inferior to Karatsuba O(n^1.585) or FFT-based O(n log n log log n) methods for large n), with the entire real benefit being human working-memory reduction (lower cognitive load, streaming additions replacing multi-step carry propagation) via constant-factor optimization, not asymptotic speedup.

aliases: Semantic Equivalence / Refinement / Contradiction / Merge Algebra

sources.note: S0902's Step 25J: attacks the one open semantic boundary left by S0901/Step 25I via a concrete relation algebra (Equal/Equivalent/Refines/RefinedBy/Contradicts/EvolvesTo/Independent), domain-relative contradiction, and a formal knowledge-merge operator with idempotence/commutativity/associativity questioned as open algebraic properties.

rows.anchor: A=(S,P,O,C,T) ... A_1=(Nexus,HasVersion,3.69.0,Production,t_1)
rows.statement: Defines the canonical assertion representation A=(Subject,Predicate,Object/value,Context,TemporalQualification), worked example A1=(Nexus,HasVersion,3.69.0,Production,t1), called 'computationally manageable.'

rows.anchor: ExactEqual(A_1,A_2)=True ... canonical serialization plus hash ... No AI is required
rows.statement: Defines deterministic ExactEqual(A1,A2), implementable via canonical serialization plus hash, worked with an identical-tuple example requiring no AI.

rows.anchor: Normalize(A_1)=Normalize(A_2) ... SemanticEquivalent(A_1,A_2)=True ... this normalization is where semantic technology enters
rows.statement: Shows two differently-phrased natural-language sentences normalize to the same canonical assertion, defining SemanticEquivalent(A1,A2)=True via Normalize() — 'this normalization is where semantic technology enters.'

rows.anchor: E_{exact}\Rightarrow E_{structural}\Rightarrow? E_{semantic} ... not necessarily the reverse
rows.statement: Defines a three-level equivalence hierarchy E_exact => E_structural =>? E_semantic (implication not guaranteed reversible) — 'semantic equivalence does not imply byte-level equality,' extending S0901's three identity relations to an ordered hierarchy.

lineage_claims.quote: E_exact => E_structural =>? E_semantic. But not necessarily the reverse.

rows.anchor: SemanticEquivalent(A_1,A_2,C,t) must include context and reference time ... CurrentVersion(2026)=3.70 ... SemanticEquivalent_{2025}\neq SemanticEquivalent_{2026}
rows.statement: Requires SemanticEquivalent(A1,A2,C,t) to include context and reference time (not optional); worked example shows 'Nexus is current' equivalence to a fixed version differs between 2025 and 2026, reinforcing the temporal model.

rows.anchor: A_2\succeq A_1 ... A_2\succ A_1 ... not equivalence
rows.statement: Defines refinement A2⪰A1 (A2 is a refinement of A1, e.g. a build-qualified version string refining a bare version), explicitly distinguished from equivalence — should be written A2≻A1, not A1=A2.

rows.anchor: A_1\preceq A_2 if every situation satisfying A_2 also satisfies A_1 ... A_{specific}\Rightarrow A_{general}
rows.statement: Formalizes refinement as a partial information order: A1⪯A2 iff every situation satisfying A2 also satisfies A1 (A_specific => A_general), worked with Version=3.69.0-build123 implying Version=3.69, computable 'if the version ontology defines the relationship.'

rows.anchor: HasVersion(x,v_1)\land HasVersion(x,v_2)\Rightarrow v_1=v_2 ... A_1\perp A_2 ... genuine contradiction
rows.statement: Defines contradiction A1⊥A2 for same subject/context/overlapping-time assertions under a functionally-exclusive predicate (HasVersion(x,v1) and HasVersion(x,v2) imply v1=v2) — 'a genuine contradiction.'

rows.anchor: HasIPAddress(Server,10.0.0.1) and HasIPAddress(Server,10.0.0.2) ... Not necessarily [contradictory] ... server could have two interfaces ... Functional(HasIPAddress)=?
rows.statement: Counterexample showing apparent contradiction (two IP addresses for one server) may not be contradictory since a server can have multiple interfaces; contradiction requires knowing whether the predicate is domain-functional (e.g. Functional(PrimaryIPAddress)=True but Functional(HasIPAddress)=False) — 'extremely important.'

rows.anchor: Contradiction(A_1,A_2,\Omega,C,T) ... a computed relation under a model
rows.statement: Generalizes contradiction to Contradiction(A1,A2,Omega,C,T) where Omega is domain ontology/rules, C context, T temporal relation — contradiction is 'a computed relation under a model,' not purely semantic.

type_signature.domain: Assertion x Assertion x Ontology x Context x Temporal

rows.anchor: LLM semantic difference \neq domain contradiction. The domain rules decide
rows.statement: Warns against a common AI error: an LLM seeing two differing IP-address facts and declaring 'contradiction' without consulting the domain model — 'LLM semantic difference ≠ domain contradiction. The domain rules decide.'

rows.anchor: A_1: Version=3.69,t_1 ... A_2: Version=3.70,t_2 ... A_1\rightarrow A_2 ... TemporalEvolution\neq Contradiction
rows.statement: Two differently-valued assertions ordered in time (t1<t2) may represent a state transition A1->A2 rather than a contradiction — 'TemporalEvolution ≠ Contradiction,' with both remaining historically valid and the current knowledge state selecting A2 as current.

rows.anchor: we do not delete A_1 ... Status(A_1)=Historical ... preserves the knowledge trajectory
rows.statement: When A2 supersedes A1 under temporal evolution, A1 is not deleted but marked Status(A1)=Historical — 'preserves the knowledge trajectory,' consistent with earlier non-destructive versioning principles.

rows.anchor: M(K_1,K_2,\Omega,C,T)\rightarrow K_3 ... preserves identity, provenance, contradictions, temporal distinctions, confidence/assessment, source independence
rows.statement: Introduces a first merge operator M(K1,K2,Omega,C,T)->K3 required to preserve identity, provenance, contradictions, temporal distinctions, confidence/assessment, and source independence — 'merging everything blindly would be dangerous.'

rows.anchor: Merge experiment 1: K_1=K_2=NexusVersion=3.69, different evidence, same context/time ... Merge does not duplicate the assertion. It aggregates support
rows.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 1: two differently-evidenced knowledge items asserting the same value, same context/time, merge to one assertion with two supporting evidence paths — 'Merge does not duplicate the assertion. It aggregates support.'

experiment.hypothesis: Redundant same-value knowledge should aggregate support, not duplicate.
experiment.setup: K1, K2 both assert NexusVersion=3.69, different evidence, same context/time.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.inputs: n/a
experiment.method: apply merge classification
experiment.result: K3: NexusVersion=3.69 with supporting E1,E2
experiment.interpretation: Confirms merge aggregates rather than duplicates identical assertions.
experiment.limitations: illustrative

rows.anchor: Merge experiment 2: K_1=3.69, K_2=3.70, same context/time ... must not arbitrarily select ... K_3: Conflict(A_1,A_2)
rows.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 2: contradictory same-context/time values must not be arbitrarily resolved — merge preserves the conflict as K3:Conflict(A1,A2).

experiment.hypothesis: Genuinely conflicting knowledge must be preserved as conflict, not silently resolved.
experiment.setup: K1=3.69, K2=3.70, same context and time.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.inputs: n/a
experiment.method: apply merge classification
experiment.result: K3: Conflict(A1,A2)
experiment.interpretation: Confirms merge never arbitrarily picks a winner.
experiment.limitations: illustrative

rows.anchor: Merge experiment 3: K_1=3.69,2025, K_2=3.70,2026 ... History: 3.69->3.70. No conflict
rows.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 3: time-ordered differing values merge into a history 3.69->3.70 with no conflict.

experiment.hypothesis: Time-ordered differing values represent evolution, not conflict.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.inputs: n/a
experiment.method: apply merge classification with temporal ordering
experiment.result: History: 3.69 -> 3.70, no conflict
experiment.interpretation: Confirms temporal evolution handling in merge.
experiment.limitations: illustrative

rows.anchor: Merge experiment 4: K_1=3.69, K_2=3.69.0-build123 ... Refinement ... retain the more specific assertion while preserving the original
rows.statement: Worked Merge Experiment 4: a general and a more specific value merge as Refinement, retaining the more specific assertion while preserving the original.

experiment.hypothesis: A refining value should be retained alongside, not replace, the general one.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.inputs: n/a
experiment.method: apply merge classification
experiment.result: Refinement; specific assertion retained, original preserved
experiment.interpretation: Confirms refinement handling in merge.
experiment.limitations: illustrative

rows.anchor: Merge(A_1,A_2)={Equivalent, Refinement, Refinement, Evolution, Conflict, Separate} ... a powerful computational classification
rows.statement: Consolidates the four merge experiments into a six-branch conditional classification: Merge(A1,A2) = Equivalent | Refinement (A1⪯A2) | Refinement (A2⪯A1) | Evolution (temporal transition) | Conflict (A1⊥A2) | Separate (none of the above).

rows.anchor: A_1: NexusVersion=3.69 and A_2: NexusCPU=8 ... Relation(A_1,A_2)=Independent
rows.statement: 'Separate'/Independent is itself important: unrelated assertions about different predicates (version vs CPU count) need no relation beyond Relation(A1,A2)=Independent.

rows.anchor: \mathcal R=\{Equal,Equivalent,Refines,RefinedBy,Contradicts,EvolvesTo,Independent\} ... should not be collapsed into one generic related relation
rows.statement: Defines a seven-member relation algebra R={Equal, Equivalent, Refines, RefinedBy, Contradicts, EvolvesTo, Independent}, explicitly warning these should not collapse into one generic 'related' relation.

rows.anchor: Equality reflexive ... Semantic equivalence reflexive/symmetric, transitivity carefully controlled ... Refinement reflexive+transitive ... Contradiction usually symmetric
rows.statement: Analyzes algebraic properties per relation: Equality is reflexive (A=A); Semantic equivalence is ideally reflexive and symmetric but transitivity must be carefully controlled since context-dependent semantic mappings can break naive transitivity; Refinement is reflexive and transitive (A⪯A; A⪯B,B⪯C=>A⪯C); Contradiction is usually symmetric (A⊥B=>B⊥A) — these properties 'can become testable invariants.'

rows.anchor: A graph of typed epistemic relations. The edge itself has semantics
rows.statement: Reframes KnowledgeOS not as a graph of objects but as 'a graph of typed epistemic relations' where the edge itself carries semantics (Equivalent/Refines/Contradicts/EvolvesTo edges), called 'a major discovery.'

rows.anchor: E_2=LLM(E_1) \Rightarrow Dependency(E_1,E_2)=True ... evidence aggregation must know provenance
rows.statement: Revisits evidence independence: two evidence items for the same assertion are not automatically independent — if E2=LLM(E1), Dependency(E1,E2)=True, so evidence aggregation must consult provenance.

rows.anchor: Original document -> Human summary / LLM summary ... not two independent observations. They are two transformations of one source ... Independent(E_human,E_LLM)=False
rows.statement: Worked example: a human summary and an LLM summary both derived from one original document are 'two transformations of one source,' not independent observations — Independent(E_human,E_LLM)=False.

rows.anchor: Database, Production test, Human inspection ... genuinely independent acquisition paths ... E_1,E_2,E_3 may provide independent support
rows.statement: Contrasting example: three genuinely separate acquisition paths (database, production test, human inspection) may provide independent support — the system 'should represent the dependency graph rather than simply count evidence items.'

rows.anchor: if E_2=f(E_1) then treating them as independent would double-count evidence ... Provenance is necessary for correct evidence aggregation
rows.statement: States the statistical consequence: naively updating P(H|E1,E2,E3) while E2=f(E1) double-counts evidence — 'a serious statistical error' — therefore 'Provenance is necessary for correct evidence aggregation.'

rows.anchor: Evidence\rightarrow DependencyAnalysis\rightarrow AssertionGrouping\rightarrow Contradiction/RefinementAnalysis\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow KnowledgeState ... significantly safer than Evidence\rightarrow AverageConfidence
rows.statement: Proposes the merge pipeline Evidence->DependencyAnalysis->AssertionGrouping->Contradiction/RefinementAnalysis->Assessment->KnowledgeState as 'significantly safer' than naive Evidence->AverageConfidence.

rows.anchor: Confidence=0.9 and 0.8 ... tempting to calculate 0.85 ... generally unjustified ... Confidence aggregation requires a defined statistical model
rows.statement: Warns against naively averaging two confidence values (0.9, 0.8 -> 0.85) since confidence is not automatically additive/averaging — requires knowing what the confidence means, which model produced it, source independence, and uncertainty representation; 'Confidence aggregation requires a defined statistical model.'

rows.anchor: Never implement: Confidence=Average(SourceConfidences) as a universal KnowledgeOS rule. Instead AssessmentModel determines how evidence is combined
rows.statement: States the architecture rule explicitly: never implement Confidence=Average(SourceConfidences) universally; an explicit AssessmentModel must determine combination.

rows.anchor: CandidateRelation(A_1,A_2,Equivalent) with GeneratedBy=LLM ... AcceptedRelation or RejectedRelation
rows.statement: An LLM-proposed equivalence between two natural-language assertions is recorded as CandidateRelation(A1,A2,Equivalent) with GeneratedBy=LLM provenance, then validated into AcceptedRelation or RejectedRelation.

rows.anchor: Semantic interpretation may be probabilistic; epistemic consequences should be governed ... a probabilistic semantic suggestion must not silently become authoritative knowledge
rows.statement: States the semantic boundary clearly: semantic interpretation may be probabilistic, but epistemic consequences should be governed — a probabilistic semantic suggestion must not silently become authoritative knowledge.

rows.anchor: O(n^2) ... partition by Subject+Predicate+Context+TimeWindow ... standard database engineering
rows.statement: Addresses naive O(n^2) pairwise-comparison cost for n assertions by partitioning/indexing by Subject+Predicate+Context+TimeWindow so comparisons occur only within candidate groups — 'standard database engineering,' illustrated reducing a 10^7-assertion comparison to small candidate sets.

rows.anchor: | Operation | Computable? | Deterministic? | ... Semantic equivalence Yes/Not necessarily ... LLM interpretation Yes/No, generally ... a very healthy result
rows.statement: Presents a 13-row computability/determinism table for identity, canonicalization, version/temporal comparison, structural refinement, contradiction, provenance dependency, evidence grouping, knowledge merge, semantic equivalence, NL normalization, LLM interpretation, and statistical evidence fusion — labeling all Computable=Yes but several (semantic equivalence, NL normalization, LLM interpretation) Deterministic=Not necessarily/No — 'a very healthy result.'

rows.anchor: SemanticCandidate\rightarrow GovernedValidation\rightarrow AuthoritativeRelation ... the non-deterministic component does not contaminate the whole system
rows.statement: States the critical conclusion: the semantic boundary is not fatal because it can be isolated via SemanticCandidate->GovernedValidation->AuthoritativeRelation, so 'the non-deterministic component does not contaminate the whole system.'

rows.anchor: Merge_K(K_1,K_2,\Omega,C,T,M)\rightarrow K_3 ... must preserve Provenance+History+Conflict+Identity
rows.statement: Defines the provisional formal knowledge-merge operator Merge_K(K1,K2,Omega,C,T,M)->K3 (K1,K2 knowledge states; Omega domain ontology; C context; T temporal semantics; M merge/assessment model), whose output must preserve Provenance+History+Conflict+Identity.

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x KnowledgeState x Ontology x Context x Temporal x MergeModel

rows.anchor: Merge(K_1,K_2) must not destroy epistemic history ... K_1 and K_2 remain reconstructable ... essential for auditability
rows.statement: States the non-destructivity invariant for merge: the operation creates a new state K3 while K1 and K2 remain reconstructable — 'essential for auditability.'

rows.anchor: Merge(K,K)=K ... a testable invariant
rows.statement: Proposes idempotence as a useful merge property (Merge(K,K)=K, or at least semantically equivalent), warning that repeated self-merging creating new substantive knowledge would be 'a serious problem' — framed as 'a testable invariant.'

rows.anchor: Merge(K_1,K_2)=Merge(K_2,K_1)? ... should not yet impose universal commutativity ... mathematical discipline prevents us from overclaiming
rows.statement: Questions whether merge should be commutative — ideal for pure knowledge-state merging, but temporal/event semantics may make order matter — explicitly declines to impose universal commutativity yet, citing 'mathematical discipline prevents us from overclaiming.'

rows.anchor: Merge(Merge(K_1,K_2),K_3) =? Merge(K_1,Merge(K_2,K_3)) ... Associativity is a design goal, not yet a proven invariant
rows.statement: Questions merge associativity, desirable because distributed ingestion benefits from associative merging but potentially failing when evidence assessments depend on intermediate state, temporal policies change, or conflict resolution is context-dependent — 'Associativity is a design goal, not yet a proven invariant... an excellent future experiment.'

rows.anchor: 25J — PASS ... Identity\rightarrow Equivalence\rightarrow Refinement\rightarrow Contradiction\rightarrow TemporalEvolution\rightarrow Merge ... How should semantic interpretation be validated? That is a much narrower problem
rows.statement: Step 25J self-verdict: PASS with a qualification — a computable algebra now spans Identity->Equivalence->Refinement->Contradiction->TemporalEvolution->Merge; the remaining unresolved question narrows from 'what is knowledge?' to specifically 'how should semantic interpretation be validated?'

rows.anchor: No semantic interpretation ... becomes authoritative merely by being generated. It becomes authoritative only through the applicable epistemic assessment and governance process ... Generation\neq Validation\neq Authority
rows.statement: States a proposed explicit KnowledgeOS invariant: no semantic interpretation (LLM, human, NLP, or other) becomes authoritative merely by being generated — only through epistemic assessment and governance — giving Generation ≠ Validation ≠ Authority, called 'one of the strongest principles in the entire architecture.'

rows.anchor: WORLD->OBSERVATION->REPRESENTATION->EVIDENCE->ASSERTION->{IDENTITY, SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION->CANDIDATE RELATION}->ASSESSMENT->KNOWLEDGE STATE->EPISTEMIC CONTRACT->ZERO->LORD->SARATHI->DECISION->ACTION->WORLD
rows.statement: Presents a refined complete pipeline diagram splitting Assertion into two parallel branches (deterministic Identity vs Semantic Interpretation -> Candidate Relation) reconverging at Assessment, then continuing through the full architecture to World — 'a remarkably coherent computational architecture.'

rows.anchor: The KnowledgeOS epistemic kernel is normal-computer computable ... You do not need quantum computing, supercomputers, exotic mathematics, enormous GPU clusters ... expensive part is primarily semantic acquisition and large-scale model inference
rows.statement: Strengthens the running computability conclusion: the epistemic kernel (Identity+Graph+Rules+Contracts+Zero+Governance+Merge+Decision) is normal-computer computable, requiring none of quantum computing/supercomputers/exotic mathematics/GPU clusters; the expensive part is semantic acquisition and large-scale model inference, not the kernel.

rows.anchor: I would not implement the full KnowledgeOS system now. We are still proving the model ... K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,\Omega,EC)
rows.statement: Explicitly declines to begin implementation, stating the mathematical closure tests must finish first, and transitions to Step 25K (Knowledge State Algebra and Closure), posing the deterministic state-transition question K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC) and listing eleven properties to test (consistency, idempotence, monotonicity, contradiction preservation, temporal evolution, invalidation, retraction, correction, replay, merge, convergence) as 'probably the most important mathematical test yet.'
